summary: Reviewed the dvpwa aiohttp application (sqli package): DAO layer, views, routes, auth utilities, middlewares, Jinja2 setup, config and templates. The app is riddled with reachable, high-impact vulnerabilities: an unauthenticated SQL injection in student creation, global disabling of template autoescaping enabling stored XSS, MD5 password hashing, and CSRF protection commented out. Overall risk is critical. Static assets (materialize/jquery) and the DB migration/fixture SQL were not deeply reviewed as they are not attacker-reachable code paths.

findings.title: Unauthenticated SQL injection in Student.create
findings.description: Student.create builds its INSERT statement with Python string interpolation (`% {'name': name}`) instead of parameterized query arguments. The `name` value flows directly from an untrusted HTTP POST body: views.students() reads `data['name']` from `await request.post()` and passes it straight into Student.create. The POST /students/ route has no authentication and, since csrf_middleware is disabled, no CSRF check either, so any anonymous attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. name=`x'); DROP TABLE marks;--` or a subquery to exfiltrate users.pwd_hash). This is the classic sink; all other DAO methods correctly parameterize.
findings.evidence: sqli/dao/student.py:42-43: q = ("INSERT INTO students (name) " "VALUES ('%(name)s')" % {'name': name}); cur.execute(q). Source: views.py:54-57 -> data = await request.post(); await Student.create(conn, data['name']). Route: routes.py:14 POST /students/ with no authorize() guard.
findings.recommendation: Use a parameterized query: `await cur.execute("INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES (%(name)s)", {'name': name})` and never build SQL with % / f-strings.

findings.title: Template autoescaping globally disabled enabling stored XSS
findings.description: aiohttp_jinja2 is initialized with autoescape=False, so every `{{ ... }}` in the templates emits raw, unescaped HTML. Attacker-controlled data is rendered directly: course review_text (course.jinja2:22), course title/description (course.jinja2:14-15), and student name (students.jinja2:16, course.jinja2:49). An anonymous user can POST a review or a student name containing `<script>` and have it executed in every visitor's/admin's browser (stored XSS). Because the session cookie is not HttpOnly, this also allows session theft.
findings.evidence: sqli/app.py:33-35 setup_jinja(app, loader=..., context_processors=[...], autoescape=False). Sink example course.jinja2:22 `{{ review.review_text }}` fed from Review.create(conn, course_id, review_text) where review_text = data.get('review_text') (views.py:121,129).
findings.recommendation: Set autoescape=True (or autoescape=select_autoescape(['jinja2','html'])) and only mark specifically trusted content safe.

findings.title: CSRF protection middleware commented out
findings.description: A working csrf_middleware exists (middlewares.py:25-38) and templates render `_csrf_token` hidden fields, but the middleware is commented out of the application middleware list. As a result none of the state-changing POST endpoints (login, create student, create course, create review, evaluate, logout) validate the CSRF token, so an attacker can forge cross-site requests that perform these actions on behalf of a logged-in victim (including an admin evaluating students).
findings.evidence: sqli/app.py:25-29 middlewares=[session_middleware, # csrf_middleware, error_middleware]. The disabled check lives in middlewares.py:25-38.
findings.recommendation: Re-enable csrf_middleware in the middlewares list so POST requests are validated against the session CSRF token.

findings.title: Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5
findings.description: User.check_password compares the stored hash to a plain unsalted MD5 of the supplied password. MD5 is fast and broken as a password KDF; combined with the SQL injection in Student.create (which can dump users.pwd_hash), all account passwords, including admin, are trivially crackable via rainbow tables/GPU brute force. Absence of a per-user salt also makes identical passwords produce identical hashes.
findings.evidence: sqli/dao/user.py:41 return self.pwd_hash == md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(). pwd_hash column is selected in User.get/get_by_username and reachable via SQLi.
findings.recommendation: Use a purpose-built password hashing function (bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2) with a per-user salt, and compare using a constant-time verify function.

findings.title: Session cookie set with httponly disabled
findings.description: The Redis session storage is instantiated with httponly=False, so the session cookie is readable from JavaScript. Given the stored XSS enabled by autoescape=False, an attacker's injected script can read document.cookie and exfiltrate the session identifier to hijack authenticated (including admin) sessions.
findings.recommendation: Use httponly=True (the default) and also set secure=True and an appropriate samesite attribute for the session cookie.

findings.title: Missing authorization on state-changing POST endpoints
findings.description: The students() handler creates records on POST with no authentication/authorization check; the UI only hides the form behind `{% if auth_user %}` in the template, but the backend never enforces it. Any anonymous client can POST directly. The same missing guard applies to courses() (views.py:83-93, POST creates a course) and review() (views.py:111-131, POST creates a review). This is also the reachability that turns the Student.create SQL injection into an unauthenticated vulnerability. Only logout uses the @authorize decorator.
findings.evidence: views.py:54-57 `if request.method == 'POST': data = await request.post(); await Student.create(conn, data['name'])` with no get_auth_user/authorize call; contrast logout at views.py:156 which is decorated with @authorize(). Routes registered without guards in routes.py:13-30.
findings.recommendation: Apply the authorize() decorator (with ensure_admin where appropriate) to all state-changing handlers instead of relying on template-level conditionals.

findings.title: Application runs with debug mode enabled
findings.description: The aiohttp Application is constructed with debug=True unconditionally (not gated on an environment/config flag). In a deployed environment this enables verbose diagnostics and can leak internal details in error output, aiding an attacker.
findings.recommendation: Drive debug from configuration/environment and default it to False in production.
